name: a6fdvd-u10-iphone-workspace-footer
goal: U10 iPhone workspace footer: a remote (paired) workspace shows one status line 'Synthetic Mac · <phone>' with one Disconnect, no 'Local project'; plus addendum: connected phone home drops the 'Signed in with Google · Sign out' line and Recent projects rows get a chevron (design record specification/designs/full-pass/README.md, section U10)

steps.title: Identify the failing behavior, expected behavior, and reproduction.
steps.evidence: Failing behavior: on a paired (online) iPhone workspace the footer shows Local project, a Shared projects line with Disconnect, and a Computer connection line with a second Disconnect; the connected home shows Signed in with Google and no chevron on Recent projects rows. Expected per design record U10 and addendum: one status line 'Connected to Synthetic Mac · Ada iPhone' with one Disconnect, no Local project, no Signed in line on the connected home, chevrons on phone rows.

steps.title: Explain why existing standardized tests missed the bug; name the scenario, fixture, lifecycle or assertion gap and reusable test change.
steps.evidence: Existing ui-remote-phone e2e covers the phone connected state at 320/390 and the paired workspace only through the lost-computer test, which asserts the compact region but not the footer's Disconnect count or Local project text. Reusable change: strengthened the same spec's connected test and added one paired-workspace test in the same file (same fixture, same viewport).

steps.title: Strengthen the existing standardized test; commit it before repair, run it failing with loop record --phase red, and preserve the assertion.
steps.evidence: Red: loop record a6fdvd-u10-iphone-workspace-footer --phase red at commit 6e456a3c04, command bunx playwright test ui-remote-phone --grep 'paired workspace|connected at' fails at 'Signed in with Google' expected 0 received 1; the paired-workspace test fails at its Connected to Synthetic Mac · Ada iPhone assertion on the same unchanged main.

steps.title: Implement the smallest repair without weakening the regression test.
Rerun the same unchanged regression test at a separate fix commit with loop record --phase green; preserve passing proof.
Run harness loop siblings to record the root cause and evaluate the same pattern across committed source.
Run relevant project checks and affected UI browser flows with fresh inspected screenshots and no unexpected browser errors; preserve diagnostics and keep pending until proof passes.
